title: Modulus of a root of unity
statement:
Every root of unity $\zeta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ has
absolute value $|\zeta|=1$ with respect to the absolute value of
[def-tw-eigenvalue]; in particular every root of unity is of weight
$0$. Moreover, for every field isomorphism
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, the
complex number $\iota(\zeta)$ also has modulus one.

proof.text: Let $m\ge1$ with $\zeta^m=1$. Applying the field isomorphism $\iota$ gives $(\iota(\zeta))^m=1$, and [lem-tw-complex-norm-root-of-unity] gives $\|\iota(\zeta)\|=1$. By the absolute-value clause of [def-tw-eigenvalue], this is $|\zeta|=1$; its weight clause then gives weight $0$, since $q^{0/2}=1$. The same norm equality is exactly the asserted modulus-one statement for the complex number $\iota(\zeta)$. The hypotheses $m\ge1$ and hence $m\ne0$ supply the nonzero-exponent assumption of the cited norm lemma.
